evals.prompt: Should our free tier be a 14-day trial or a limited free plan?
evals.expected_output: Should explain the depth-versus-time principle: a time limit cuts people off before attachment, a usage limit cuts them off at peak attachment. Should cite Notion's 300 blocks. Should also give the conversion trade-off: freemium converts at 2-8% (median 4.5%) while an opt-out trial with a credit card converts at 35-55% but generates far less top of funnel. Should tie the choice to whether they need volume or revenue.
assertions: Explains metering by depth rather than time
Gives both conversion ranges with tags
Notes the credit-card trial's much higher conversion
Notes the trade-off in top-of-funnel volume
Ties the recommendation to the user's stage need

evals.prompt: How do I figure out what to charge?
evals.expected_output: Should give the Van Westendorp four questions and a sample size (150-200 single audience, 100-150 per segment). Should give the 10-30% of value created heuristic. Should stress segmenting first since value perception varies enormously by vertical and size. Should note GitLab, Confluent, and MongoDB each needed many pricing iterations to pass $1B ARR.
assertions: Gives the four Van Westendorp questions
Gives the 10-30% of value created heuristic
Notes that nobody gets pricing right first time
Does not give a single number without inputs
